title: Dynamics 365 Field Service: Scheduling Operations Agent suggests optimised technician schedules
summary: The briefing is supported by the roadmap record and Microsoft's preview documentation. The enablement requirements, consumption billing, control paths, API operations and qualified optimisation limits were verified.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap target is March CY2027.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "March CY2027"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is June CY2025.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "June CY2025"

claims.claim: The record lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists the Web platform.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The record associates the feature with Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365) and Dynamics 365 Field Service.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365)", "Dynamics 365 Field Service"]

claims.claim: The roadmap describes access from the Copilot side pane anywhere in the Field Service application.
claims.quote: Users can access the feature from the Copilot side pane anywhere within the Dynamics 365 Field Service application.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes optimising for technician utilisation or work order priority.
claims.quote: You can direct Copilot to optimize for the business goal you want, such as maximizing technician usage or work order priority.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes enablement by admins for end users.
claims.quote: Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users

claims.claim: The agent suggests improved schedules for one or more technicians.
claims.quote: The Scheduling Operations Agent in Dynamics 365 Field Service optimizes the schedules of one or more technicians at the same time.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents interactive and batch optimisation modes.
claims.quote: The Scheduling Operations Agent supports two ways to optimize schedules:

claims.claim: Interactive optimisations can start from the schedule board, a resource list or Copilot.
claims.quote: Interactive optimizations let a dispatcher select up to five resources from the schedule board, a resource list, or Copilot

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: Interactive runs support up to five resource capacity points, counting each capacity point of a resource separately.
claims.quote: Up to 5. A resource with a capacity greater than 1 counts as one resource for each capacity point.

claims.where: What's changing: first and second paragraphs
claims.claim: The dispatcher reviews an interactive suggestion and chooses whether to apply it.
claims.quote: Review the agent's suggested schedule before you apply it.

claims.claim: Batch optimisations run asynchronously.
claims.quote: The optimization runs asynchronously, so you can continue working while the agent processes the request.

claims.claim: A scope defines the resources, unfulfilled requirements and existing bookings for a batch optimisation.
claims.quote: A scope defines which resources to optimize, which unfulfilled requirements to consider, and which existing bookings the agent can change.

claims.claim: A goal defines the objectives and constraints for a batch optimisation.
claims.quote: A goal defines the objectives and constraints for the optimization.

claims.claim: A batch plan combines a scope and goal with a time range.
claims.quote: A plan combines the scope and goal with a time range.

claims.claim: Batch plans can run on demand or on a recurring schedule.
claims.quote: Run a plan on demand or on a recurring schedule.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy; controls[3].note; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A batch plan can hold results for review or apply them automatically without that review step.
claims.quote: Whether the results are applied automatically or held for you to review depends on the plan's Apply method

claims.claim: The overview says the agent never moves bookings marked Do Not Move, with booking-level overrides separately acknowledged.
claims.quote: The agent never moves bookings that are marked Do Not Move

claims.claim: The agent respects technician working hours.
claims.quote: it respects each technician's working hours and breaks.

claims.claim: The agent respects technician breaks.
claims.quote: it respects each technician's working hours and breaks.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn documents the agent as preview, rather than silently treating the roadmap target as a launched release.
claims.quote: This is a preview feature.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft says preview features are not meant for production use.
claims.quote: Preview features aren't meant for production use and may have restricted functionality.

claims.claim: Learn says the agent is available in Field Service's Azure regions except Azure Government and China.
claims.quote: The Scheduling Operations Agent is available in the same Azure regions as Dynamics 365 Field Service, except Azure Government and China.

claims.claim: Learn describes a gradual rollout across supported Azure regions.
claims.quote: The feature is rolling out gradually across the supported Azure regions.

claims.claim: Learn directs readers to Universal Resource Scheduling version history for rollout dates.
claims.quote: Rollout dates are listed in the release schedule for Universal Resource Scheduling.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: An administrator must set up and turn on the agent before dispatchers can use it.
claims.quote: Before dispatchers can use the agent, an administrator must set it up in your environment.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Setup requires an administrator role in Dynamics 365.
claims.quote: You have an administrator role in Dynamics 365.

claims.claim: Turning on the agent enables both interactive and batch optimisations.
claims.quote: Turning on the agent enables both interactive and batch optimizations.

claims.claim: No automation for this agent's enablement toggle is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Scheduling Operations Agent enable toggle API msdyn schedulingparameter; Scheduling Operations Agent toggle Dataverse enable. Opened soa-setup, faqs-soa and the Dataverse msdyn_schedulingparameter reference; no documented operation or value format identified as this agent's toggle.

claims.claim: The agent toggle is in Field Service app > Resources > Scheduling Parameters > Resource Scheduling > Agents.
claims.quote: Change to the Resources area and go to Scheduling Parameters > Resource Scheduling. Go to the Agents tab and turn on Scheduling Operations Agent (Preview).

claims.claim: User roles are assigned in Power Platform admin center > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Manage security roles.
claims.quote: Select your environment, and then go to Settings > Users + permissions > Users. Select a user, and then select Manage security roles.

claims.claim: The printed v9.0 POST to systemuserroles_association/$ref with a roles reference assigns a Dataverse security role to the specified user.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The two Scheduling Operations Agent roles are additive rather than replacements for existing roles.
claims.quote: They're additive, so assign them alongside a user's existing roles rather than replacing them.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; controls[3].note
claims.claim: Scheduling Operations Agent Administrator grants creation of scopes, goals and plans.
claims.quote: Scheduling Operations Agent Administrator | Administrators who create scopes, goals, and plans | Create, edit, and delete scopes, goals, and plans, and view optimization results.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; controls[1].note
claims.claim: Scheduling Operations Agent User is the role for dispatchers running optimisations.
claims.quote: Scheduling Operations Agent User | Dispatchers who run optimizations

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Users also need underlying scheduling-table access, for example through Field Service - Dispatcher.
claims.quote: Each user also needs a role that grants access to the underlying scheduling tables, such as bookable resources, bookings, and resource requirements - for example, a dispatcher role like Field Service - Dispatcher.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: The agent runs as an application user in Scheduling Operations Agent Team.
claims.quote: The agent runs as an application user that belongs to the Scheduling Operations Agent Team.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Changes use the combined permissions of the running user and application user, and both must have record access.
claims.quote: Each change the agent makes uses the combined permissions of the user who runs the optimization and the agent's application user, so both must have access to the affected records.

claims.claim: The application user can read and write standard scheduling tables by default.
claims.quote: By default, the agent's application user can read and write the standard scheduling tables.

claims.claim: Custom, Field Service or Project Operations table access is granted through matching roles on Scheduling Operations Agent Team.
claims.quote: If your optimizations use custom tables, Field Service or Project Operations tables, or queries that reference other tables, assign the matching security roles to the Scheduling Operations Agent Team

claims.claim: Column-level security on queried columns requires adding the agent team to the matching field security profile.
claims.quote: If you use column-level security (field security profiles) on any columns that your scopes or queries reference, also add the Scheduling Operations Agent Team to the matching field security profile.

claims.claim: Without that field security profile access the agent might ignore filter conditions and return incorrect results.
claims.quote: Otherwise, the agent might ignore filter conditions on those columns and return incorrect results.

claims.claim: Optimization Method is configured in Field Service app > Resources > Booking Settings > Booking Statuses > booking status.
claims.quote: Open the Field Service app and go to the Resources area. Select Booking Settings > Booking Statuses. ... For each booking status, set the Optimization Method property

claims.claim: The printed PATCH updates a bookingstatus row using the documented bookingstatuses entity set and Dataverse JSON update syntax.
claims.quote: Update ... PATCH /bookingstatuses(bookingstatusid) ... See Update

claims.claim: Writable msdyn_optimizationmethod uses 192350000 for Optimize, 192350001 for Do Not Move and 192350002 for Ignore.
claims.quote: LogicalName | msdyn_optimizationmethod ... 192350000 | Optimize ... 192350001 | Do Not Move ... 192350002 | Ignore

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment: Autonomy; Governance guidance
claims.claim: An unset booking status Optimization Method is treated as Do Not Move.
claims.quote: If you don't set this field, the agent treats all bookings in that status as Do Not Move.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Optimize allows the agent to move or delete bookings, making changes to scheduling records.
claims.quote: Optimize: The agent can move or delete bookings with this status to generate an optimal schedule.

claims.claim: Booking status methods govern preservation or overriding of bookings.
claims.quote: Do Not Move: The agent must preserve the estimated arrival time ... Ignore: The agent can override bookings with this status and move or create new bookings on top of them.

claims.claim: An individual booking's Optimization behavior overrides the method implied by its booking status.
claims.quote: When you set Optimization behavior on an individual booking, the agent uses that setting for the booking instead of the behavior that the booking's status optimization method implies.

claims.claim: A new batch plan's Apply method is configured in Resource Scheduling app > Settings > Optimization > Scheduling Plans > New.
claims.quote: In the Settings area of the Resource Scheduling app, under Optimization, select Scheduling Plans, and then select New. ... For Apply method, select Review before apply or Apply automatically.

claims.claim: PATCH of msdyn_schedulingoptimizationplans with msdyn_applymethod 859530000 sets Review before apply.
claims.quote: PATCH /msdyn_schedulingoptimizationplans(msdyn_schedulingoptimizationplanid) ... LogicalName | msdyn_applymethod ... 859530000 | Review before apply

claims.claim: Results awaiting review expire at the optimisation window's start or 72 hours after running, whichever comes first.
claims.quote: Results that are waiting for review expire at the start of the optimization window or 72 hours after the request runs, whichever comes first.

claims.claim: The agent warns before applying a batch result if bookings, requirements or resources changed since the request ran.
claims.quote: If bookings, requirements, or resources changed since the request ran, the agent warns you before applying.

claims.claim: Always match time window can remove an expired-promise booking from the suggested schedule before the dispatcher applies it.
claims.quote: If you select this option and a booking in the optimization range has an expired promise window, the agent deletes that booking from the suggested schedule.

claims.claim: Priority Value accepts 1 to 100 and determines relative priority.
claims.quote: It accepts numbers between 1 and 100. The higher the number, the higher the priority.

claims.claim: The agent ignores Level of Importance.
claims.quote: The agent ignores the Level of Importance field.

claims.claim: Widely separated priority values can make the highest-priority bookings nearly always included despite inefficient placement.
claims.quote: This results in Emergency bookings nearly always being included in the result, regardless of how inefficient the placement is.

claims.claim: Equipment, Pool and Facility resource types are unsupported.
claims.quote: It doesn't support resources of type Equipment, Pool, and Facility.

claims.claim: Requirement groups are unsupported.
claims.quote: It doesn't support requirement groups or multiday requirements (requirements that are related to requirement detail records).

claims.claim: Multiday requirements related to requirement detail records are unsupported.
claims.quote: It doesn't support requirement groups or multiday requirements (requirements that are related to requirement detail records).

claims.claim: Four or more resource breaks per workday or shift produce an error.
claims.quote: A resource can have up to three breaks per work day or shift. With four or more breaks, the agent returns an error.

claims.claim: Field Service version 8.8.133.214 or newer is required.
claims.quote: Your environment is updated to Field Service version 8.8.133.214 or newer

claims.claim: Universal Resource Scheduling version 3.12.149.15 or newer is required.
claims.quote: Universal Resource Scheduling version 3.12.149.15 or newer.

claims.claim: Location and map settings must be turned on.
claims.quote: Location and map settings are turned on for your environment.

claims.claim: Each resource the agent should consider needs Display on schedule board set to Yes.
claims.quote: set the following properties for each bookable resource that you want the agent to consider: Display on schedule board must be Yes.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: first paragraph; Open questions
claims.claim: The setup prerequisites and roadmap record do not name a dispatcher's user licence.
claims.quote: Searched: Scheduling Operations Agent data processing region movement consent license dispatcher. Read the roadmap record and soa-setup in full: prerequisites name product versions, Location and map settings and an administrator role, not a dispatcher user licence.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and cost; summary; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The agent uses consumption-based billing measured in Microsoft Copilot Studio credits.
claims.quote: Scheduling Operations Agent and other Copilot and agent capabilities in Dynamics 365 use Microsoft Copilot Studio credits ... These capabilities use consumption-based billing, charging per use, and credits are the billing units that measure usage.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Why it matters; rationale: cost
claims.claim: One optimisation request consumes credits according to the number of resources included.
claims.quote: For the Scheduling Operations Agent, a single optimization request consumes credits based on the number of resources it includes, so optimizing more resources at once uses more capacity.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Prepaid capacity uses Copilot Studio credit pack subscriptions.
claims.quote: The prepaid capacity model uses Copilot Studio credit pack subscriptions, which are a licensing option for Microsoft Copilot Studio that you purchase in advance.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go is supported through an Azure subscription.
claims.quote: To set up pay-as-you-go billing, you first need an active Azure subscription. Link the subscription to your Power Platform environment

claims.claim: Both billing models can be used in the same environment.
claims.quote: You can use both billing models in the same environment.

claims.claim: Prepaid capacity is consumed first.
claims.quote: Prepaid capacity is consumed first.

claims.claim: The setup page says both models require linking the Dynamics 365 environment to a Power Platform environment.
claims.quote: Both models require that you link your Dynamics 365 environment to a Power Platform environment.

claims.claim: The setup page says depleted quota makes AI capabilities unavailable until capacity is added.
claims.quote: When the quota is depleted, AI capabilities are unavailable until more capacity is added.

claims.claim: For pay-as-you-go the setup page directs readers to Microsoft Cost Management in Azure portal for usage and budgets.
claims.quote: For pay-as-you-go, use Microsoft Cost Management in the Azure portal to view detailed usage and adjust spending limits, or budgets, to free up more capacity.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio credit capacity and usage are visible in Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: You can view Copilot Studio credit capacity and usage for both prepaid capacity and pay-as-you-go billing in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The setup page gives no numerical per-optimisation credit rate.
claims.quote: Searched: Scheduling Operations Agent credits limit cap consumption rate. Read soa-setup in full: it states consumption depends on resource count, without a numerical credit rate.

claims.claim: No separate credit cap or credit-use switch is documented specifically for Scheduling Operations Agent.
claims.quote: Searched: Scheduling Operations Agent credits limit cap consumption rate; Scheduling Operations Agent consumption limits. Opened soa-setup and Manage Copilot Credits and capacity for Copilot Studio; the latter covers Copilot Studio agents without identifying this Dynamics agent as covered.

claims.claim: Interactive runs have a limit of 120 jobs.
claims.quote: Jobs (existing bookings and open requirements) | Up to 120.

claims.claim: Interactive optimisations have a 72-hour window limit.
claims.quote: Optimization window | Any 72-hour window in the future.

claims.claim: Batch optimisations support up to 50 resources.
claims.quote: Resources | Up to 50.

claims.claim: Batch optimisations support up to 4,000 jobs.
claims.quote: Jobs (existing bookings and open requirements) | Up to 4,000.

claims.claim: Batch optimisations support up to 2,000 bookings per resource.
claims.quote: Bookings per resource | Up to 2,000.

claims.claim: Batch optimisations have a maximum 14-day range.
claims.quote: Optimization range | Up to 14 days.

claims.claim: Recurring plans have a minimum interval of 30 minutes.
claims.quote: Saved scheduling plans support a minimum recurrence interval of 30 minutes.

claims.claim: Scheduling Operations Agent Team is configured in Power Platform admin center > environment > Settings > Teams.
claims.quote: In the Power Platform admin center, select your environment, and then go to Settings > Teams. Select the Scheduling Operations Agent Team.

claims.claim: The agent's Learn pages do not specify its processing location or whether it requires cross-region data-movement consent.
claims.quote: Searched: Scheduling Operations Agent data processed; Scheduling Operations Agent data processing region movement consent. Opened soa-overview, soa-setup, faqs-soa and geographical-availability-copilot; the platform page does not identify this agent.

claims.claim: The PATCH examples use documented Dataverse v9.2 JSON update syntax with Content-Type: application/json and If-Match: *.
claims.quote:
PATCH [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/accounts(00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001) HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
OData-MaxVersion: 4.0
OData-Version: 4.0
If-Match: *
